clue.text: Fight to stop batting record being set with it

parts.note: a batsman who is batting is said to be in

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so the fight sits inside the record

parts.note: CD, a compact disc, is a record
a row is a fight or quarrel

explanation.surface: A scrap breaks out to prevent a cricket scoring record being set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' puts ROW inside CD, and IN goes in front. 'set' looks like part of the record story but is a noun here: the fashionable set.
explanation.definitionFit: The fashionable clique that is with it, a social set in the know, is called the in-crowd.

clue.text: Cadmium on coin that's been moved beyond reach

indicators.note: letters that have been moved are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemist describes metal on a coin that has been shifted out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been moved' rearranges CADMIUM ON COIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot be contacted is out of reach, held without communication.

clue.text: Devastated about being not considered

parts.note: c, circa, means about
a rushed decision is one not considered

explanation.surface: Someone shattered at being passed over.
explanation.definitionFit: Crushed means overwhelmed with dismay, synonymous with devastated.

clue.text: Illusory works appeal to some

definitions.meaning: abstract art built on optical illusions
this kind of art pleases some viewers but not all

explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s movement of optical illusion paintings, a kind of art liked by some people.

clue.text: Revolutionary Head's training was effective

definitions.note: the rotating cutting tip, with the possessive standing for is

parts.note: drill is military training
bit, as brakes bit, means took effect

explanation.surface: A radical headteacher's instruction programme worked.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'revolutionary' is not a rebel but something that spins; the 's is read as is.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill's cutting tip turns at the head of the tool, so it is a spinning head.

clue.text: Delegates: mark that short stripper in grass skirts!

indicators.note: skirts means goes round the edge of, so the shortened insect surrounds the mark
short says the last letter of the insect is lopped off

parts.note: a locust strips the grass and crops bare
M stands for the mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a stand-in exotic dancer wearing a hula outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts LOCUST to LOCUS, and 'skirts' wraps that round M. The stripper is not a dancer at all but the crop-eating insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors or clergy who stand in for others act as deputies, loosely delegates for the regular holder.

clue.text: What's left in colliery cage last to be lifted a little

indicators.note: to be lifted says the hidden letters are read backwards
a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mine's last cage of coal is hoisted a short way up the shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to be lifted' reads the run upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is what someone has left in a will.

clue.text: His ascent rocked Highland area

indicators.note: rocked means shaken about, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A climber's ascent of a Scottish mountain wobbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocked' rearranges HIS ASCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Caithness is a historic county at the far north of the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: No good slicing mushroom with mixed stock

indicators.note: slicing means cutting into, so the letters go inside the mushroom

parts.note: a morel is an edible mushroom

explanation.surface: A bad cook ruins mushrooms by slicing them into a mixed broth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slicing' puts NG inside MOREL. 'stock' looks like soup but means breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog of mixed breeding has mixed stock or ancestry.

clue.text: Celebrate clinching publicity with vintage campaigning

parts.note: a cru is a vineyard or vintage of wine

indicators.note: clinching means holding fast, so the publicity is held inside the celebration

parts.note: to sing is to celebrate in song
an ad is publicity

explanation.surface: A party with good wine and press coverage marks a successful campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clinching' puts AD inside SING; CRU comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusading means fighting vigorously for a cause, which is campaigning.

clue.text: Here's an idea that's not new to me

definitions.meaning: the exclamation someone makes when struck by a sudden thought
the reply of someone already aware of what they are being told

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both as a cry of inspiration and as a weary reply showing prior knowledge.

clue.text: County player with hand on glossy publication

parts.note: West is one of the four players at bridge, each dealt a hand
glam means glamorous, glossy
an organ is a newspaper or journal

explanation.surface: A footballer posing with a magazine shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: WEST GLAMORGAN was a county in south Wales from 1974 to 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a former administrative county of Wales, centred on Swansea.

clue.text: Explode a myth that I refuse to believe

indicators.note: exploding something blows it apart, so the letters fly into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone debunking a myth they will not accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explode' rearranges A MYTH.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of disbelief comes from the idiom about eating one's hat if a claim proves true.

clue.text: Alert to sound, surrounded by sticks, join battle

indicators.note: surrounded by says the alert goes inside the word for sticks

parts.note: locks means sticks or jams fast
a horn is a warning device one sounds

explanation.surface: Soldiers hear the alarm and, armed with sticks, charge into the fray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' puts HORN inside LOCKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stags fighting interlock antlers, so the idiom means to engage in conflict.

clue.text: Fail to secure enough support

definitions.meaning: whimsically, to pin something too little, falling short of fastening it
to prop up or give a foundation to

explanation.definitionFit: To shore up a structure from below is to give it support; the playful reading is pinning too little.

clue.text: They make fast speed when sailing under marine hazard

indicators.note: in a down clue under places the speed below the hazard

parts.note: a reef is a danger to shipping
knots measure speed at sea

explanation.surface: A yacht travelling quickly near rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Square knots used by sailors securely fasten two ropes, making them fast.

clue.text: Match official needs delay to change registration

parts.note: ref is short for referee
a lag is a delay

explanation.surface: A referee needs time to update a player's registration.
explanation.definitionFit: To reflag a ship is to register it under a different national flag.

clue.text: Chap vainly rolling up to bash sups his shandy at the back

indicators.note: a bash is a party or blow, either way a riotous reshaping of the letters
at the back means take the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man staggering home after a party drinks his shandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the back' gives Y from shandy, and 'bash' rearranges SUPSHIS with it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth he was condemned to push a boulder uphill forever, only for it to roll back.

clue.text: Stole quietly away?

indicators.note: away says the quiet letter goes missing from the word for stole

parts.note: pinched means stole
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, crept off slowly, while PINCHED with its P sent 'away' builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving off by small degrees is stealing away by tiny stages.

clue.text: Gas caught by replacing head of exhaust

indicators.note: replacing head of says the first letter of the word is swapped out

parts.note: shatter means exhaust or tire out
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Fumes trapped after a car's exhaust part is changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing head of' swaps the S of SHATTER for C.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is to talk idly at length, which is chatter.

clue.text: Family like to reserve quiet area in city

indicators.note: to reserve is to hold, so the family and like hold the quiet sound

parts.note: kin means family
as means like
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Relatives keeping a hushed spot in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reserve' puts SH inside KINAS, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinshasa is the capital city of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

clue.text: Start off with cheerful humour — Pythonesque?

indicators.note: start off means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: sanguine means cheerful and was one of the four medieval humours

explanation.surface: A Monty Python sketch opens in good spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pythonesque' suggests Monty Python, but means like a python snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguine means snakelike, so it describes something resembling a python.

clue.text: Publicity on computer switched on around day's beginning

indicators.note: around says the alert word goes round the letter

parts.note: switched on means alert or aware

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of day

explanation.surface: Morning computer advertising aimed at a savvy audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' gives D, which 'around' places inside AWARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that displays advertising on a computer is advertising-supported, a form of publicity.

clue.text: Lament regular deficiencies

definitions.meaning: playfully, a shortfall every day: a lack each day

explanation.definitionFit: The archaic exclamation is an expression of grief, and split up it suggests a daily shortage.

clue.text: Saving goods, seconds from catastrophe? Pray don't bother!

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe within, so the picked letters hold the goods
seconds from means take the second letter of each of the following words

parts.note: G is good, so goods is two of them

explanation.surface: An exhortation not to fret about rescuing possessions from disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds from' takes A, R, O from cAtastrophe, pRay, dOn't; 'Saving' puts GG inside, between A and RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for trouble or aggravation, that is, bother.

clue.text: Parting words after one gets out for a pair

indicators.note: gets out means the letter for one leaves the word

parts.note: adieux are goodbyes
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Farewells said after a cricketer is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets out' suggests cricket but takes I from ADIEUX.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means for two, as in a meal for two people.

clue.text: Part that closes in flower turned yellowy colour

parts.note: a plant in flower is out

indicators.note: turned says the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A bloom turning a golden shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes RO from OR. 'flower' tempts as a river, but it means blooming.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing section of a piece of music or a show is its outro, opposite of the intro.

clue.text: Stuff burning with that is very fulfilling!

indicators.note: to stuff one thing with another is to fill it, so the burning holds the rest

parts.note: aching and burning both describe pain
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Feeding the fire is deeply satisfying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' puts IEV inside ACHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Accomplishing something is fulfilling an aim; the definition is clued as a gerund phrase.

clue.text: Swears after fumbling catch in the deep

indicators.note: fumbling means handling clumsily, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fielder curses after dropping a catch near the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fumbling' rearranges SWEARS. 'the deep' is a cricket fielding position, but here it is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrasse is a sea fish that anglers might land from the ocean.

clue.text: Four by four observed circling Roman square by junction

indicators.note: circling says the observed word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: seen means observed
IX is nine in Roman numerals, a square number
a T is a junction shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A four-wheel drive vehicle seen going round a square near a road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts IXT inside SEEN. 'Four by four' looks like a car but is multiplication.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplying four by four gives this number.
